judge_context: The fix belongs in create_reverse_many_to_one_manager.get_prefetch_queryset in related_descriptors.py, where the parent instance is manually set on each prefetched child. An idiomatic change is a two-line guard using the existing field cache API (self.field.is_cached(rel_obj)) rather than new bookkeeping, changes to Model.get_deferred_fields, or special-casing deferred loading in prefetch_related_objects.

case_items.name: Guard is conditional and covers the one-to-one variant
case_items.name_zh: 仅在已缓存时跳过回填，并考虑一对一情形
case_items.question: Does the fix skip assigning the parent onto each prefetched child only when that child already has the relation cached (e.g. field.is_cached(rel_obj)), so plain prefetches without a nested prefetch still populate the reverse relation without extra queries, and does it consider the OneToOneField variant the issue describes (user.profile.user) in addition to the reverse ForeignKey path (user.profile_set.all()[0].user)?

criteria.perfect: Assignment is guarded by an is_cached-style check on the child; the reverse relation is still populated when not cached; the one-to-one path (ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset) is either guarded the same way or explicitly analysed in the final report.
criteria.accept: Reverse-FK path is correctly guarded but the one-to-one variant from the issue is neither handled nor mentioned.
criteria.bad: Reverse assignment is removed unconditionally (plain prefetch now triggers extra queries), the guard is based on deferred-field hacks / copying deferred fields, or the guard is inverted.
